A4 is driven LOW as ground and A5 HIGH as 5 V in software, so the sensor is powered from the analog pins. The ADXL3xx pin VDD is the catalogue port VCC.
The tutorial notes that some ADXL3xx boards are 3.3 V only and 5 V could damage them. The circuit shown supplies about 5 V, following the tutorial's SparkFun breakout.

ATmega328P pin use: 1 RESET, 2 RXD, 3 TXD, 7 VCC, 8 GND, 9 XTAL1, 10 XTAL2, 17 MOSI, 18 MISO, 19 SCK, 20 AVCC, 22 GND. Pin 21 (AREF) is left unconnected.
Bootloader burning (ArduinoISP): Uno pin 10 to RESET, 11 to MOSI, 12 to MISO, 13 to SCK, plus 5V and GND. Wires 1-4 are removed after burning, as the text says.

Uploading: the Arduino's own microcontroller is removed. Uno pin 0 (RX) goes to ATmega pin 2 and Uno pin 1 (TX) to ATmega pin 3. These are straight, not crossed, because the removed chip leaves pins 0 and 1 connected to the USB-serial chip. The Uno RESET goes to ATmega pin 1. The pictures show these wires only roughly, so this follows the standard Arduino arrangement.

The 10k resistor pulls RESET (pin 1) up to 5V on the bottom + rail. The crystal sits between pins 9 and 10 via the two blue wires. Each 22 pF capacitor goes from a crystal leg to ground (bottom - rail).

Top rails are fed from the Uno 5V and GND and linked to the bottom rails by wires 11 and 12. Wires 9 and 10 take VCC and GND to pins 7 and 8 from the bottom rails. Wires 7 and 8 take AVCC and GND to pins 20 and 22 from the top rails.

I kept the nano1 3V3 connection and did not change the graph, because the E8 warning is not a real problem for this manual. The catalogue's 4.5-21 V supply range is for powering the board in. This tutorial powers both boards over USB (5 V), which is within range. The 3V3 pin is the board's 3.3 V regulated output, so it is not a power input and does not need 4.5 V. The circuit image labels the pin '3V' and uses it only as the pull-up voltage for SDA and SCL. Moving the pull-ups to 5 V or VUSB would be the real error here, because the Nano 33 IoT's I/O pins are 3.3 V only and not 5 V tolerant.

SCL is A5 and SDA is A4, as the text states. The SCL and SDA lines cross in the image without connecting.
Only the reader's 3V3 pin feeds the pull-ups. The writer's 3V3 is not connected.
GND is a single direct jumper from reader GND to writer GND. The Nano Every GND and GND2 pins are joined inside the board, so GND is used.
The USB cables plug into each board's USB port. The computer end is not modelled as a part.
The image draws Nano 33 BLE-style boards, but I kept the Nano Every the text names.
